## NEUTROPENIC FEVER--PATIENT IS A CANDIDATE FOR ORAL THERAPY
## Can the patient be treated with oral therapy?
[Link to a scoring tool that identifies low risk patients for oral therapy](orzid2-gmenu-neut-fever-scoring-tool)
## Treatment
Preferred:
## Inpatient

[Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO q12h ($) [R,DI] <AND> amoxicillin-clavulanate](orz-set-abx-cipro-500mg-q12h-amox-clav-875-125-q12h)
875/125 mg PO q12h ($) [R]
Alternative:
[Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO q12h ($) [R,DI] <AND> Clindamycin 300mg po q6h ($) [H,O]](orz-set-abx-ciproflox-500mg-po-bid-clindamycin-300mg-po-q6h)
## Outpatient

[Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO BID ($) [R,DI] <AND> amoxicillin-clavulanate](orz-set-abx-op-cipro-500-bid-amox-clav-875-125-bid)
875/125 mg PO BID ($) [R]
[Non-VA order for above](orz-set-abx-nv-cipro-500-bid-amox-clav-875-125-bid)
Alternative:
[Ciprofloxacin 500mg po bid ($) [R,DI] <AND> Clindamycin 300mg po qid ($) [H,O]](orz-set-abx-op-cipro-500-bid-clindamycin-300-qid-x7days)
Non-VA order for above
References:
Freifeld AG Clinical Infectious Disease 2011, 52: 427-431
Taplitz RA, J Clin Oncol 2018, 36: 1443-1453
Sanford: Neutropenia, Febrile, Low-Risk
NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines, Prevention and Treatment of Cancer-
Related Infections. Version 1.2019. nccn.org
